chunks: Although Allah gives time to the oppressor, His catch would not spare him. He watches him on the passage of his way and the position of that which suffocates the throats.

By Allah in Whose power my life lies, these people (Mu‘āwiyah and his men) will overcome you not because they have a better right than you but because of their hastening towards the wrong with their leader and your slowness about my right (to be followed).
People are afraid of the oppression of their rulers while I fear the oppression of my subjects.
ai.seo_question: Why did Imam Ali say Muawiya's men would overcome the Muslims despite the truth being with Ali?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) elucidates that the triumph of Mu'awiya's faction stems not from superior legitimacy but from their swift adherence to falsehood and the companions' delay in recognizing his authority, a dynamic rooted in the concept of *sari'ah* (haste) in Shia political theology. He concludes with a poignant inversion of the typical ruler-subject dynamic, expressing his unique anxiety over oppressing his own people, thereby highlighting the weight of *adl* (justice) and *mas'uliyyah* (accountability) inherent in his leadership.
